title: A Case of the Mondays: Punter Tears, Firing Odds, and a Very Well-Fed Saturday in Charlottesville
paragraphs: Well, the actual games haven't kicked off yet as of this collection of sources, but that hasn't stopped the Commanders content machine from running at full RPM, and honestly the biggest story of the week has nothing to do with Saquon Barkley or the Eagles' defensive line. It's Tress Way. The man has punted for this franchise for thirteen years, longer than some current Commanders players have been legally allowed to drive, and he told reporters, "I am pretty sure this is gonna be my last season." Jeremy Reaves reportedly got emotional just talking about it, which tells you everything about how beloved this guy is in that locker room. Punters are supposed to be the anonymous guys who jog on, kick, jog off, but Way turned himself into a genuine institution, and the fact that half the beat is writing eulogies for him before Week 1 even happens is a testament to that.

Meanwhile Dan Quinn is, per the oddsmakers, apparently the favorite to be the first head coach fired in the entire NFL this season, which is a wild thing to be true before a single snap of the year has been played. Quinn's response to that kind of noise was refreshingly blunt when he told The Washington Post, "What are you going to actually fucking do about it?" Say what you want about the man's seat temperature, but that is a T-shirt slogan waiting to happen. It's also just funny that Washington's coach is somehow simultaneously the guy fans are nervous about and the guy who sounds the calmest person in the building.

On the injury front, Daron Payne popped up on the report as limited with a knee, which is the kind of news that makes an entire fanbase's stomach drop slightly before remembering it's only Week 1 and everybody is beat up in September. He's joined in the limited column by Jacory Croskey-Merritt, K'Lavon Chaisson and Odafe Oweh, while Javon Kinlaw was a full participant despite a back injury, which either means Kinlaw is built differently or the Commanders medical staff has really generous definitions of "full." On a happier note, Jayden Daniels was named a team captain alongside Terry McLaurin, Frankie Luvu, Jeremy Reaves and, fittingly, Tress Way in what might be his final marching-off-into-the-sunset lap.

The Daniels storyline heading into Philadelphia is less about box-score numbers and more about a mindset reset. Dan Quinn told The Post the team literally cut tape of every scramble Daniels took in 2025 to teach him when to slide instead of lowering a shoulder into a linebacker, saying, "I don't think he had that part of his game in order, and he does now." That's either a great coaching adjustment or the most passive-aggressive game film session in franchise history, and possibly both. McLaurin, for his part, is preaching ball security ahead of a Philly defense that will be teeing off on a shaky Washington offensive line missing Laremy Tunsil, and given that stat about Daniels and McLaurin sharing the field for only 13.9 percent of snaps last year, Commanders fans would very much like to see that number go up before it becomes a trivia question nobody wants to answer.

Elsewhere in the league, the NFL kept doing NFL things, which is to say chaos found teams that absolutely did not need more of it. The Patriots, fresh off getting throttled in the Super Bowl, somehow managed to give away a game to the Seahawks with their backup quarterback in at the controls, which is not exactly the redemption arc New England was hoping to sell this year. And in Australia, of all places, the Rams reportedly struggled with fumbles that got blamed on jet lag, a theory NBC Sports Washington's JP Finlay was, in his own words, not sure he bought. Somewhere a Rams equipment manager is quietly Googling flight times just to double check.

Back in Ashburn, there's also a lighter side to all this preseason hand-wringing: Northwest Stadium rolled out a new DMV-inspired food lineup for the year, which means Commanders fans will at least be eating well while they nervously watch the offensive line try to hold up against Philadelphia. Priorities, as always, in order.

Now, allow me to hop over to Scott Stadium for a moment, because while Washington was still just previewing its opener, my Cavaliers already played theirs, and I got to watch the whole thing from the President's Box, which is a phrase I will never tire of typing because my wife works up there and I benefit enormously from that fact every single home Saturday. There is truly nothing like watching UVA take care of business while balancing a small plate of catered food in one hand and a very reasonably poured drink in the other, all thanks to a job that has nothing to do with football but everything to do with my personal happiness on fall weekends. Virginia beat NC State 34-8, and it was the kind of laugher that let me relax into the good snacks by the second quarter instead of nervously pacing, which, frankly, is the entire dream of college football fandom realized.

Next up for the Cavaliers is Norfolk State, which should mean another low-stress Saturday of catered football watching, and I intend to treat it exactly that way. Elsewhere in the sport, seventh-ranked Miami put up 77 points on Florida A&M, a reminder that college football's point totals can occasionally look like they were generated by a video game left on easy mode. Back on Commanders business, though, the vibes remain appropriately jittery heading into Philly, proof that no amount of good stadium food in Charlottesville can fully cure Washington fans of Week 1 nerves. Here's hoping Sunday goes better than the oddsmakers currently expect.
